clue.text: Very attractive, ample — not left disconnected

parts.note: fit is slang for very attractive

indicators.note: 'not left' tells us the letter for left is missing from the word before it

parts.note: ample means full

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a gorgeous, curvy figure, noting it lacks any leftward lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes L (left) from FULL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitful sleep or progress comes in broken bursts, so it is disconnected rather than continuous.

clue.text: Possibly care to wear ermine, Travers?

indicators.note: to wear is to have around oneself, so the fur goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: ermine is a white fur

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be in another order

explanation.surface: Would the playwright Ben Travers be willing to put on an ermine robe?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' and 'to wear' do the work; 'ermine' suggests a robe but is simply fur. Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was a writer of stage farces, an example of a farceur, a farce writer.

clue.text: Experience loss of testes almost — daft A&E aberration

indicators.note: an aberration is a departure from the normal, so the letters stray from their order
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: A&E is the hospital Accident and Emergency department, giving the letters A and E

explanation.surface: A patient fears losing his testicles because of a foolish error in the A&E department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of testes, giving TESTE; 'aberration' rearranges TESTE, DAFT and AE. A&E is a British hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste defeat is the idiom for experiencing being beaten, suffering a loss.

clue.text: Not struck with church divorce

parts.note: unhit means not struck

explanation.surface: A couple separates without any blows, and the church has to approve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorce' is the verb here, as in separating one thing from another.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or detach, which is to divorce one thing from another.

clue.text: Backward class welcomes religious examination

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the assembled letters from the end to the start
to welcome is to take in, so the class word holds the religious word inside it

parts.note: a class is a sort or kind
pi is informal British slang for pious or religious

explanation.surface: A slow class in school takes in a religious studies exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' builds SOPIRT and 'Backward' turns it round. The Tripos is the honours exam system at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the final honours examination for a Cambridge degree, a specific kind of examination.

clue.text: Rogue racehorse fails to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the horse word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a trotter is a horse bred for trotting races

explanation.surface: A rogue horse refuses to leave the starting gate at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' drops the opening T of TROTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is an old-fashioned British word for a cad or scoundrel.

clue.text: Navigational aid prototype ring inserted in echo locator

parts.note: a pilot version is a trial or prototype

indicators.note: inserted in means the ring goes into the next word

parts.note: a bat finds its way by echolocation
O is the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A prototype sonar device has a ring fitted inside its echo-locating unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echo locator' sounds like sonar gear but is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot boat carries the pilot who guides ships through harbours, so it helps navigation.

clue.text: Traditional Scotsman's ready to be put in one?

definitions.text: Traditional Scotsman's ready to be put in one?

parts.words: Traditional Scotsman's ready to be put in one?
parts.note: ready here is slang for cash, and a kilted Scotsman keeps his money in a pouch worn at the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is not the adjective but slang for money, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch worn on the front of a kilt, holding a Scotsman's money.

clue.text: Introduction to "Alice in Wonderland" so sullied a sports venue

indicators.note: sullied letters are spoiled and thrown out of order
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The opening of Alice in Wonderland was so defiled by a sports arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction to' takes A from Alice; 'sullied' rearranges A, WONDERLAND and SO. Lansdowne Road was the Dublin rugby stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Lansdowne Road in Dublin was the home ground of Irish rugby and football, a sports venue.

clue.text: See 15
Get to know about Hard Spike, marksman with Ohio's top force

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an ear of corn is a spike of grain
William Tell is the legendary marksman who shot the apple off his son's head

indicators.note: Ohio's top is the first letter of that word

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A tough-guy sharpshooter called Hard Spike teams up with Ohio's top police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' reads like a nickname but is the ear of a cereal plant; 'top' takes the first letter of Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear tell of something is an idiom for learning of it through report or rumour.

clue.text: See 2
Understands salts show a reaction to punch?

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
old salts and tars are both slang for sailors

explanation.surface: A chemist grasps how certain salts behave when a punch, the drink, is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salts' and 'punch' look like chemistry and drinks, but salts are sailors and the punch is a blow to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is punched hard may see stars, the idiom for briefly glimpsing flashes of light.

clue.text: Kitty cherishes Cher's dancing like a kid who has no class

definitions.text: like a kid who has no class

indicators.note: to cherish is to hold close, so the kitty word holds the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, as in a shared fund

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Kitty adores watching the singer Cher perform her dance routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes RESCH, held by 'cherishes'. 'Kitty' looks like a girl's name but is the shared pot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A preschool child is too young for school, so is not yet in any class.

clue.text: Suspect evildoing of singer in smart novel

indicators.note: in places the singer inside the jumbled letters
novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was a famous jazz singer

explanation.surface: Someone suspects wrongdoing by a singer appearing in a clever new novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' gives SMRAT and 'in' places the singer within it; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for sensing that something is wrong or dishonest.

clue.text: Blue wing's unpunctuated surrender

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling down or sad
a wing can be an arm, and arm's written without its apostrophe gives the plural form

explanation.surface: A depressed wing-forward plays on, careless about punctuation, and finally gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpunctuated' asks for ARM'S with the apostrophe dropped, so the letters run on as ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down arms is to stop fighting and give up, an idiom for surrendering.

clue.text: Price, taking goblin about, gets go ahead

indicators.note: taking means the price word takes the other pieces inside itself

parts.note: a fee is a price charged
an elf is a small mischievous creature like a goblin
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone pays a fee to hire a goblin and is then given permission to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' splits the price after its second letter; the definition is the imperative 'go ahead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are friendly invitations telling someone they have permission to do something.

clue.text: Sharp finished superior road

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
over means finished, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A sharp operator has finished building a better road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' means higher up, not better: the road is raised above another.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyover is a road carried over another on a bridge, so it is literally above.

clue.text: Undergoing education makes sense beyond any used in 10, 12, 16 25, 2 11 and 14?

definitions.text: sense beyond any used in 10, 12, 16 25, 2 11 and 14?

parts.note: being in something means undergoing it, as in 'in training'
tuition means teaching or education

explanation.surface: A student in school realises there is a sense beyond the five used in other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The other answers use hearing, sight, feel, taste and smell; this is the so-called sixth sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is often called the sixth sense, knowing without using hearing, sight, touch, taste or smell.

clue.text: After raise, went out, romantically briefed

indicators.note: after tells us the following piece comes behind the raise piece

parts.note: to up is to raise, as in upping the price
dated means went out with someone romantically

explanation.surface: After a pay rise, someone went on a romantic date and was filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefed' means given the latest information.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone updated has been told the latest news, which is to have been briefed.

clue.text: Out of condition spy broadcast at a less busy time

parts.note: off means past its best or out of condition, as with food

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out to listeners, so the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: to peek is to spy or take a quick look

explanation.surface: An unfit spy goes on air at a quiet hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' asks for PEEK said aloud, which sounds like PEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak hours are those of lower demand, such as cheaper rail travel outside rush hour.

clue.text: Chateau Nice farm houses organisation with minor concerns

indicators.note: houses means the phrase holds the name of the organisation within it

explanation.surface: A farm attached to a chateau near Nice is home to a small charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across chateaU NICE Farm. 'minor' means children, not small: UNICEF is the UN children's fund.
explanation.definitionFit: UNICEF is the United Nations agency for children, so minors are its concern.

clue.text: Hole ship for the viewer's enhancement

parts.note: an eye is a small hole, as in the eye of a needle
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A cabin porthole on an ocean ship gives passengers a better view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' means the eye itself, which make-up enhances.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up that outlines and enhances the eye, which is the organ we view with.

clue.text: Spotted thing gets sick, as doomed species do

parts.note: a die has spots marking its numbers
feeling off means feeling unwell or sick

explanation.surface: A spotted creature falls ill, the way animals do on their way to extinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted thing' suggests an animal, but it is a dice cube marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Species heading for extinction die off, the phrasal verb for dwindling until all are dead.

clue.text: Playfully delicate life abused and shortened

indicators.note: abused letters are mistreated and knocked out of order
shortened means the word loses both ends, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A delicate life is mistreated and cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges LIFE into ELFI, and 'shortened' trims AND to N.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small, light and mischievous, like an elf, so playfully delicate.

clue.text: Film director wants Cruise for African location

parts.note: James Ivory is the film director of A Room with a View
to coast is to cruise along without effort

explanation.surface: A director wants Tom Cruise to star in a film shot in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' looks like the actor Tom Cruise but is a verb meaning to coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory Coast, or Cote d'Ivoire, is a country on the West African coast.

clue.text: See 16
Make to look a bit like a rodent sanction?

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

parts.words: Make to look a bit like
parts.note: the suffix -ify forms verbs meaning to make like something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether making a face look rat-like counts as an approved procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue treats the answer as a made-up verb, to make rat-like.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty is to approve it formally, giving it official sanction.

clue.text: Port's responsible for smug Dan's kind heart

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase is its inner letters, which spell the port

explanation.surface: A harbour town is said to be the reason a smug man called Dan has a kind heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across smuG DAN'S Kind. Gdansk is a Baltic port in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Polish seaport on the Baltic Sea.
